author: ojiudezue
title: Retired the excursion kill switch; S1's borrow check = borrow record OR self-discharging nudge/compromise timers only
summary: The v5.88.0 back-out option 'Restore thermostats after temporary changes' was removed so every borrow always records a row. S1's borrow gate reads only the self-expiring registry row plus the nudge restore timer, nudge in-flight set and compromise timer; token dicts and predictor/egress leftovers were dropped. Built by a new Tier-3 agent (ura-super-builder, Fable 5.1 low effort).
why: All four Tier-3 reviews showed leftover markers (banking token after the 2 h sweep, _last_precool_zones with Zone Intelligence off) outlive their borrow and re-create the §9.1 lockout. The only reason those fallbacks existed was the kill-switch-OFF case, where no row is written; the option had never been turned off and single-install means no back-compat scaffolding. Operator proposed separating 'record' from 'restore'; retiring the knob achieved it by deleting code instead of adding branches to borrow code.
alternatives_considered: Gate (f): respect manual when the kill switch is OFF — simpler but an unexplained exception to the rule
Keep the knob but always record rows, gating only the restore path — adds logic to begin_excursion, which the operator asked to keep clean
implications: Emergency back-out for borrow bookkeeping is now a release rollback. Any gate-(e) evidence added later must self-discharge or be bounded by the row's stale_ts. Fix-up round 2 also makes the arrester's own timers check for live borrows at fire time (pre-existing leak where a compromise/revert could turn AC back on during an egress pause).
revisit_trigger: A borrow-bookkeeping defect in production that would have needed the off-switch.
